rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He first reads سعى literally as movement through the land for corruption—raiding and theft not undertaken to exalt God’s word—and takes ليفسد as its purpose.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { في الأرض } تأكيد لمدلول { سعى } لرفع توهم المجاز من أن يراد بالسعي العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, سعى can mean intending and devising corruption; ليفسد is then its object, with a communicative lam and implicit أن, as in 2:185 and 9:32.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { سعى } مجازا في الإرادة والتدبير أي دبر الكيد لأن ابتكار الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line attributed to Juʾz ibn Kulaib al-Faqʿasi illustrates wanting expressed with a lam; al-Marzūqī reads تبغى ليستاد as seeking to capture, with the infinitive as object.
rows.anchor: وقول جزء بنن كليبب الفقعسي : تبغى ابن كوز والسفاهة كاسمها ليستاد منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An eloquent speaker may use a causal lam where its action is both the cause and object; the object reading is recoverable by construing an implicit أن.
rows.anchor: وأقول : إن هذا الاستعمال يتأتى في كل موضع يقع فيه مفعول الفعل علة للفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في الأرض attaches to سعى and specifies activity among the people of their land; the repeated فيها explicates the first phrase and reinforces it.
rows.anchor: ويكون قوله : { في الأرض } متعلقا بسعى لإفادة أن سعيه في أمر من أمور أهل أرضكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the yāʾ read with ḍamma, the verb means that he destroys the crops and offspring.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ويهلك الحرث والنسل } بضم الياء أي يتلفه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الحرث means crops, while النسل means animal young and derives from wool falling away and separating.
rows.anchor: والحرث هنا مراد منه الزرع ، والنسل أطفال الحيوان مشتق من نسل الصوف نسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers taking crops and offspring as a proverbial image for destroying what sustains people, who relied on cultivation and livestock, rather than as only those two things.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن إهلاك الحرث والنسل كناية عن اختلال ما به قوام أحوال الناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says crops and offspring allude specifically to what al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq did.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحرث والنسل هنا إشارة إلى ما صنع الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever reading is chosen, the verse makes such a perpetrator liable to punishment in the afterlife; the closing clause warns and rebukes him.
rows.anchor: فالآية دالة على أن من ينتسب في مثل ذلك صريحا أو كناية مستحق للعقاب في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating divine love means negating approval, since love as an affective inclination toward appreciation cannot apply to God; he says approval means will for his school and the Muʿtazilites, an issue tied to the creation of acts.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نفي المحبة نفي الرضا بالفساد ، وإلا فالمحبة وهي انفعال النفس وتوجه طبيعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An all-powerful God who disapproves of an act can punish its perpetrator, because no obstacle can prevent Him.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن القدير إذا لم يرض بشيء يعاقب فاعله ، إذ لا يعوقه عن ذلك عائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destroying crops is called corruption even if they belong to polytheists, because losing the earth’s goods harms everyone; fighting may destroy only things that enable destruction and aggression.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الزرع والحرث للمشركين : لأن إتلاف خيرات الأرض رزء على الناس كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption destroys benefits that are wholly or predominantly useful: milk is wholly useful, and firewood predominantly so; destroying marginal benefits such as wine, or things with no benefit such as pests, is not corruption.
rows.anchor: والفساد ضد الصلاح ، ومعنى الفساد : إتلاف ما هو نافع للناس نفعا محضا أو راجحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption disables the wise purposes for which God created things for people. War destroys a predominant harm, so burning homes or cutting trees is prohibited unless retaining them would strengthen the enemy, prolong fighting, and risk Muslim defeat; necessity is limited to its measure.
rows.anchor: ومن أجل ذلك نهي عن إحراق الديار في الحرب وعن قطع الأشجار إلا إذا رجح في نظر أمير الجيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an admonisher reminds him of what entails mindfulness of God, he becomes angry at the admonition.
rows.anchor: أي وإذا وعظه واعظ بما يقتضي تذكيره بتقوى الله تعالى غضب لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخذ originally means taking by hand, then commonly means taking control, overpowering, receiving, or enveloping; here جاهلية pride has enveloped him. The cited Quranic uses include 9:5, 6:42, and 3:81.
rows.anchor: والأخذ أصله تناول الشيء باليد ، واستعمل مجازا مشهورا في الاستيلاء قال تعالى : { وخذوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العزة is the holder’s belief that no one can overpower him or challenge his speech, based on his standing among his people and their strength; Samawʾal’s verse illustrates their inability to contradict his group.
rows.anchor: والعزة صفة يرى صاحبها أنه لا يقدر عليه غيره ولا يعارض في كلامه لأجل مكانته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also means strength and dominance, often grounded in tribal numbers among Arabs, though bravery can replace numbers; the proverb and Samawʾal’s verse illustrate this, and the adjective appears at 2:209.
rows.anchor: ومنه العزة بمعنى القوة والغلبة وإنما تكون غالبا في العرب بسبب كثرة القبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in العزة is referential: it denotes familiar pre-Islamic pride that bars its owner from accepting blame or correction; being seized by it implies refusing counsel.
rows.anchor: ف ( أل ) في ( العزة ) للعهد أي العزة المعروفة لأهل الجاهلية التي تمنع صاحبها من قبول اللوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment: sinful, unjust pride. This qualification distinguishes it from the praiseworthy pride affirmed at 63:8; it blocks admonition and leaves him attached to habitual sin.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { بالإثم } الباء فيه للمصاحبة أي أخذته العزة الملابسة للإثم والظلم وهو احتراس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat follows from that state. Since حسب means sufficiency and what suffices is normally fit for someone, he uses it for recompense; Abu al-Ṭayyib’s line illustrates fitting measure.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحسب هو الكافي كما سيجيء عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannam is a proper name for the punishment abode and is indeclinable; some grammarians explain this by definiteness and femininity, while most explain it by definiteness and foreign origin, making etymological inquiry unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وجهنم علم على دار العقاب الموقدة نارا ، وهو اسم ممنوع من الصرف قال بعض النحاة للعلمية والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some derive the name from Arabic جهم, ‘abhorrence,’ proposing patterns with doubled nūn or a repeated nūn; the author answers that rare patterns are attested in دونك and حفنكى.
rows.anchor: ومن جعله عربيا زعم أنه مشتق من الجهم وهو الكراهية فزعم بعضهم أن وزنه فعنل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other derivations say the name was borrowed and Arabized from Persian كهنام or Hebrew كهنام.
rows.anchor: ومن قال : أصلها بالفارسية كهنام فعربت جهنم . وقيل أصلها عبرانية كهنام بكسر الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a deep well ركية جهنم does not prove an Arabic derivation: the well is likened to Hell as an immensely deep, fire-filled pit.
rows.anchor: وأما قول العرب ركية جهنم أي بعيدة القعر فلا حجة فيه ، لأنه ناشىء عن تشبيه الركية بجهنم

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل أو أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: A poem attributed uncertainly to Waraqa ibn Nawfal or Umayya ibn Abi al-Ṣalt, lamenting Zayd ibn ʿAmr, depicts Hell as a dark, fiery oven; the passage links this image to 2:24 and says hadith likewise describes it.
rows.anchor: قال ورقة بن نوفل أو أمية بن أبي الصلت يرثي زيدا بن عمرو بن نفيل وكانا معا ممن ترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith likewise depicts Hell as a fiery oven; the Quran names it fire in many places and says people and stones fuel it, as discussed at 2:24.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء وصف جهنم في الحديث بمثل ذلك وسماها الله في كتابه في مواضع كثيرة نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مهاد is what is prepared for sleeping; calling Hell a bed is mockery because sinners are thrown into it and their sides and backs meet it.
rows.anchor: والمهاد ما يمهد أي يهيأ لمن ينام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in العباد may be comprehensive: God shows compassion to all servants, with differing shares in this life and the next; disbelievers receive worldly health and provision but not hereafter compassion.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن التعريف في قوله ( العباد ) تعريف استغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, العباد may be definite by reference to servants of the kind just described, those who give themselves seeking God’s pleasure.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التعريف تعريف العهد أي بالعباد الذين من هذا القبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that أل substitutes for a possessive suffix, as in 79:41; servants when attached to God can mean His specially near servants, as at 15:42.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( أل ) عوضا عن المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coda’s relevance is that these people gave themselves to God as His servants, so He is compassionate to them. If the referent is general, naming servants instead of using a pronoun makes the coda an independent maxim and explains their devotion.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة هذا التذييل للجملة أن المخبر عنهم قد بذلوا أنفسهم لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If من refers specifically to Suhayb, the coda means God is compassionate to the servants of whom Suhayb is one; Romans and then Banu Kalb enslaved him and did not pity his torture for God, but God did when he became His servant.
rows.anchor: وإن كان ما صدق ( من ) صهيبا رضي الله عنه فالمعنى والله رءوف بالعباد الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage teaches believers to discern inner realities and not be deceived by appearances before testing: a person may speak sweetly and look good while concealing evil and plotting harm.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية وهي قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may construe the command to ‘know’ as treating their knowledge as nonexistent because they fail to act on it: by not promptly entering the religion, violating its rulings, or resenting the Messenger’s treaty.
rows.anchor: ولك أن تجعل قوله : { فاعلموا } تنزيلا لعلمهم منزلة العدم لعدم جريهم على ما يقتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase excuses them while directing them to entrust the matter to God, who revealed the treaty for a benefit; it is no weakness, since God is mighty and wise, and Badr showed His care for His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال تعالى : { من بعد ما جاءتكم البينات } إعذار لهم ، وفيه إشارة إلى أنهم يجب عليهم تفويض العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if the passage concerns entering or remaining in Islam, slipping means conduct against that command and the proofs are the Messenger’s miracles; al-Razi quotes Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar that punishment follows proof, not the individual’s certainty, which is not excused if evidence suffices.
rows.anchor: نقل الفخر عن ( تفسير القاضي عبد الجبار ) دلت الآية على أن المؤاخذة بالذنب لا تحصل إلا بعد البيان

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf tells of a reader who read ‘God is forgiving, merciful’ after slipping; a Bedouin objected that a wise speaker would not mention forgiveness at a lapse, since that encourages it.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الكشاف ) روي أن قارئا قرأ هذه الآية فإن الله غفور رحيم فسمعه أعرابي فأنكره

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi, citing Tafsir al-Naqqash, attributes a similar anecdote about the reading to Kaʿb al-Ahbar.
rows.anchor: وفي القرطبي عن ( تفسير النقاش ) نسبة مثل هذه القصة إلى كعب الأحبار

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi reports al-Asmaʿi’s story: a Bedouin challenged a reader who ended the theft verse with ‘God is forgiving, merciful’; when it became ‘mighty, wise,’ he approved, reasoning that God prevailed and judged by cutting, whereas forgiveness would not cut.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطيبي عن الأصمعي قال كنت أقرأ : والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this verse, īlāʾ became a legal term for the specifically defined oath abstaining from intercourse with one’s wife. The cited line and 24:22 illustrate usage; there is no need to posit ellipsis or transference.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فالإيلاء بعد نزول هذه الآية ، صار حقيقة شرعية في هذا الحلف على الوصف المخصوص .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial lam marks the respite as a concession for husbands and conveys choice: waiting is not obligatory, so they may resume before four months.
rows.anchor: ومجيء اللام في { للذين يؤلون } لبيان أن التربص جعل توسعة عليهم ، فاللام للأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb takes من rather than its usual على because it includes the sense of distancing oneself; من marks figurative separation or starting point.
rows.anchor: وعدى فعل الإيلاء بمن ، مع أن حقه أن يعدى بعلى ؛ لأنه ضمن هنا معنى البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: النساء means wives, as in 2:222. Attaching an oath of abstention to ‘women’ is like attaching legal permission or prohibition to persons, as at 4:23 and 2:173.
rows.anchor: والنساء : الزوجات كما تقدم في قوله : { فاعتزلوا النساء في المحيض } ( البقرة : 222 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarabbus is waiting for something outside the waiter’s control; fuller discussion is deferred to 2:228. Annexing the wait to four months means ‘during’ them, like ‘the plotting of the night’ at 34:33.
rows.anchor: والتربص : انتظار حصول شيء لغير المنتظر ، وسيأتي الكلام عليه عند قوله تعالى : { والمطلقات يتربصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting للذين يؤلون before the predicate تربص emphasizes the concession granted to husbands and builds anticipation for the subject.
rows.anchor: وتقديم { للذين يؤلون } على المبتدأ المسند إليه ، وهو تربص ، للاهتمام بهذه التوسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاءوا means return to intercourse; its object is omitted as obvious. Return is effected by expiating the oath, as prescribed in 5:89.
rows.anchor: و { فاءوا } رجعوا أي رجعوا إلى قربان النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four-month limit is set by God, but its wisdom is unknown to people and the author does not claim to know it. A third of a year may count as a long interval because a third is treated as substantial, as with an estate and the Prophet’s advice to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr about fasting the year.
rows.anchor: وقد خفي على الناس وجه التأجيل بأربعة أشهر ، وهو أجل حدده الله تعالى ، ولم نطلع على حكمته

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Some scholars explain the deadline through a story of ʿUmar, which Ibn Kathir attributes to Malik’s Muwattaʾ from ʿAbd Allah ibn Dinar; Ibn ʿAshur cannot find it in the extant recensions he lists and allows it may be in another one.
rows.anchor: وعزا ابن كثير في ( تفسيره ) روايتها لمالك في ( الموطأ ) عن عبد الله بن دينار . ولا يوجد هذا في الروايات

rows.speaker: أبو الوليد الباجي
rows.claim: Al-Baji includes the account in his Muwattaʾ commentary al-Muntaqa without attributing it to any particular Muwattaʾ recension.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر هذه القصة أبو الوليد الباجي في شرحه على الموطأ المسمى ( بالمنتقى ) ، ولم يعزها

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In the account, ʿUmar hears a wife sing of a long, lonely night; she says her husband was sent to Iraq. Women say a wife can endure two months, weakens at three, and reaches her limit at four; one version says he asked Hafsa. He orders commanders to recall soldiers after four months and send replacements.
rows.anchor: أن عمر خرج ليلة يطوف بالمدينة يتعرف أحوال الناس فمر بدار سمع امرأة بها تنشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بعولة is the plural of بعل, ‘husband’; بعل originally meant ‘master’ and is an old Semitic word. The Canaanite/Phoenician deity Baal is named at 37:125.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وبعولتهن } . البعولة جمع بعل ، والبعل اسم زوج المرأة . وأصل البعل في كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husband was called بعل because he held authority over the marital bond and was regarded as a woman’s owner and master. As family law developed from Abraham onward, that ownership sense diminished and Arabic زَوْج came to name either spouse fairly, since each completes a pair.
rows.anchor: وسمي به الزوج لأنه ملك أمر عصمة زوجه ، ولأن الزوج كان يعتبر مالكا للمرأة وسيدا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran usually calls spouses زَوْج; exceptions occur in accounts of earlier peoples, as at 11:72, or when recalling male authority, as at 4:128 and here, where the husband has the right of return.
rows.anchor: وقد عبر القرآن بهذا الاسم في أغلب المواضع ، غير التي حكى فيها أحوال الأمم الماضية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view derives بعل from ‘male’: the deity Baal symbolizes masculine power, and a tree that grows without irrigation is also called بعل.
rows.anchor: وقيل : البعل : الذكر ، وتسمية المعبود بعلا لأنه رمز إلى قوة الذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural بَعُولة has the pattern faʿūla, built on the regular faʿūl plural of faʿl and given an extra tāʾ marbūṭa by attested usage to suggest a collective, as in فحولة and ذكورة; it adds emphasis to group plurality.
rows.anchor: وجاء جمعه على وزن فعولة ، وأصله فعول المطرد في جمع فعل ، لكنه زيدت فيه الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in بعولتهن refers to the previously mentioned revocably divorced women. They are called divorced because husbands initiated divorce, although divorce breaks the bond; during the waiting period they occupy a middle status, so ‘their husbands’ is a metaphor based on their prior status.
rows.anchor: وضمير { بعولتهن } ، عائد إلى ( المطلقات ) قبله ، وهن المطلقات الرجعيات كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting period gives men room to regret and seek reconciliation, as 65:1 says, ‘perhaps God will bring about something after that’; this resembles the rule of īlāʾ.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل الله مدة العدة توسعة على المطلقين ، عسى أن تحدث لهم ندامة ورغبة في مراجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During the waiting period divorced women are between the status of wives and strangers; calling their former husbands بَعُولة is a transparent metaphor based on their prior status, like continuing to call grown wards ‘orphans’ at 4:2.
rows.anchor: وعلى اعتبار هذه الحالة الوسط أوقع عليهم اسم البعولة هنا ، وهو مجاز قرينته واضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك points to the waiting period’s duration: husbands may return their wives during the three quruʾ, not afterward. The verse legislates reconciliation while the divorce waiting period lasts.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بقوله : { ذلك } إلى التربص بمعنى مدته ، أي للبعولة حق الإرجاع في مدة القروء الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the verse both establishes reconciliation and urges divorced husbands to pursue it: since one or both spouses may want reunion, men are urged to overlook causes of divorce, being more likely to judge patiently while women are more prone to anger and refusal.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن هذا ليس مجرد تشريع للمراجعة بل الآية جامعة لأمرين : حكم المراجعة ، وتحضيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رد was discussed at 2:217; here it means returning to married life, or reconciliation.
rows.anchor: والرد تقدم الكلام عليه عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik treats ‘returning’ literally, supporting the view that divorce legally severs the marriage bond.
rows.anchor: وتسمية المراجعة ردا يرجح أن الطلاق قد اعتبر في الشرع قطعا لعصمة النكاح ، فهو إطلاق حقيقي على قول مالك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومن وافقوه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and his followers read ‘return’ figuratively: during the waiting period the bond is already on a path to dissolution at its end, and reconciliation turns it back from that course.
rows.anchor: وأما أبو حنيفة ومن وافقوه فتأولوا التعبير بالرد بأن العصمة في مدة العدة سائرة في سبيل الزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition ‘if they intend reconciliation’ exhorts husbands to seek repair; it does not restrict the right to return.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { إن أرادوا إصلاحا } شرط قصد به الحث على إرادة الإصلاح ، وليس هو للتقييد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لَهُنّ cannot refer to the nearest ‘divorced women,’ who no longer have mutual marital rights; it refers to wives implied by ‘returning them.’ Accordingly الرجال means their husbands, as ‘the man of a woman’ means her husband, like ‘his wife’ at 11:71 and 11:81.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون ضمير { لهن } عائدا إلى أقرب مذكور وهو ( المطلقات ) ، على نسق الضمائر قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to wives in 2:226: since unjustified īlāʾ harms their rights, the general rule follows that specific context. The discourse moves from wives to divorced women and, through return, back to them as wives, a ring composition.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يعود الضمير إلى النساء في قوله تعالى { للذين يؤلون من نسائهم } ( البقرة : 226 ) بمناسبة أن الإيلاء من النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of equal rights fits the preceding mention of īlāʾ, which can involve husbands asserting control over the marital bond at women’s expense.
rows.anchor: والمناسبة أن في الإيلاء من النساء تطاولا عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses symmetrical ellipsis: its full sense is that women have against men rights like the rights men have against women, with each half elided because the other supplies it.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية احتباك ، فالتقدير : ولهن على الرجال مثل الذي للرجال عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women’s rights are stated first because men’s claims over women were long familiar and accepted, while women’s rights were neglected or left to a wife’s standing with her husband; Islam established them, and this verse is a central foundation.
rows.anchor: وكان الاعتناء بذكر ما للنساء من الحقوق على الرجال
